text:
anya: FYI the onboarding sample app started failing in edge preview after publishing the canary that tightened the exports map. stack: 
SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'

drew: That usually means a CJS process pulled an .mjs. Did the canary remove main/module fallbacks? paste package.json snippet.

anya: snippet: {
  "name":"@redwood/onboard-sample",
  "version":"0.2.0-canary",
  "exports":{
    "./feature":{"import":"./dist/feature.mjs","require":"./dist/feature.cjs"}
  },
  "types":"dist/index.d.ts"
}

rafa: Looks like no root export and no ./package.json export. Many bundlers and edge runtimes prefer explicit root entry and package.json export to avoid fallback resolution.

anya: repro: sample-app CI uses edge-preview image; local node16 passed but CI edge fails. ci-bot shows 3/3 failures.

ci-bot: CI sample-app / integration failed in edge-worker. link: internal/ci/98765

drew: Quick fix: add root export and ./package.json export plus keep main/module fields. e.g. exports: { ".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"}, "./package.json":"./package.json", "./feature":{...} } and package.json top-level main/module/types.

rafa: Also ensure we publish both .cjs and .mjs and include d.ts files. Add a small smoke test that does `require()` and `import()` against npm pack artifact.

anya: I'll open a patch and publish a canary to validate edge CI. will report back here.
